title: Rec.709 vs Rec.2020: Color Gamut Is Not HDR
description: Rec.2020 covers a wider color gamut than Rec.709, but does not automatically mean HDR. Learn what to check before exporting an SDR sharing copy on iPhone.
direct: Rec.2020 defines a wider color gamut than Rec.709. That means it can represent a broader palette of colors, not that every Rec.2020 video is HDR. Choose an export for the receiving workflow, and check both its color primaries and transfer function.

cards.gamut.heading: A bigger palette, not more pixels
cards.gamut.body: Rec.709 is the standard-gamut HDTV reference. Rec.2020 uses wider-gamut red, green and blue primaries. These color definitions are separate from your export resolution: selecting 4K alone does not tell you how its colors are encoded.
cards.hdr.heading: Why Rec.2020 does not automatically mean HDR
cards.hdr.body: Color gamut describes the palette; dynamic range describes the span of brightness. Rec.2020 primaries also appear in Rec.2100 HDR systems using PQ or HLG transfer functions. A primaries label alone is not enough to identify the brightness encoding.
sections.choice.heading: Which should you export?
sections.choice.body: Use Rec.709 SDR when the recipient or editor requests standard SDR delivery. Keep a supported wide-gamut HDR workflow when HDR delivery is required. Converting to a smaller gamut can change colors outside that gamut. Changing a metadata label is not a substitute for color conversion, and exporting Rec.709 footage as Rec.2020 cannot recover colors never captured.

steps.import.text: For a Rec.709 SDR sharing copy of supported iPhone HDR footage, import the video into our VideoFix: HDR Video Converter and choose Convert HDR to SDR. The published App supports H.264 MP4 output with Rec.709 SDR color.
steps.check.text: Keep the original for editing. Export a short copy and check bright areas, saturated objects and playback in the receiving app. Conversion re-encodes the video. The first three conversions are free; unlimited conversions require a purchase.
